messages:
erin: Heads-up — need to lock the Dedicated Capacity PRD acceptance criteria and SLA targets by EOD Fri. Customer A is pushing for a reserved contract with 99.95% availability and 95th pctl latency <= 120ms for text gen requests. Can we map this to realistic throughput/instance sizing?

maya: @erin is that 99.95 the bar they need for all regions or just NA? they mentioned EU but weren't specific.

ajay: For NA-only, 99.95 is doable but depends on overprovisioning vs. smarter fallbacks. If we set target instances = sustained qps * headroom(1.5) + burst buffer, dedicated pool size balloons.

noah: SRE note: we shouldn’t promise 120ms 95th for requests > 1k tokens without KV-cache warm. We can guarantee 120ms for requests < 512 tokens at config X. For longer sequences, we need different SLO buckets.

lucy: telemetry will need per-route 95/99 pctl and error-rate signals. Acceptance test should include synthetic traffic that mixes 20/50/30 short/med/long seqs and verifies throughput and tail latency.

ajay: Proposed autoscale policy (draft):
```yaml
autoscale:
  metric: token_qps
  target: 800  # tokens/sec per reserved shard
  cooldown_sec: 120
  min_shards: 4
  max_shards: 32
  burst_capacity: 2_shard_equiv
  fallback_policy: route_to-hosted
```
This keeps steady state predictable but gives some burst headroom.

erin: Draft acceptance criteria (suggested):
```
1) Functional: Dedicated pool serves pinned model variant and honors model version pinning.
2) Availability: 99.95% global availability for NA reserved pools (measured at route-level) over a 30d window.
3) Latency: 95th pctl latency <= 120ms for requests <=512 tokens under steady-state load (defined by perf tests).
4) Throughput: Sustained throughput of X requests/sec per shard (value to be calculated from perf run).
5) Autoscale: Policy scales up before latency degradation >10% and scales down with cooldown >=120s.
6) Degradation: On capacity shortfall, traffic must gracefully fallback to hosted variants within 5s with no silent failures.
7) Observability: Dashboards and alerting for shard-fill, token_qps, tail latency, error-rate; test hooks for canary failover.
```

maya: Good list. Two questions: who owns the calculation for X (requests/sec per shard)? and what's the customer-facing rollback behavior when we fallback to hosted? need wording for contracts.

ajay: I'll own perf runs and calculate X by Thu. For contract language on fallback: we return 503 with header `x-redwood-fallback: hosted` and increment `fallback_count` metric; support page documents expected latencies.

noah: Also call out edge case: network partition in region — fallback must prefer cross-region rather than immediate hosted fallthrough to avoid capacity blowups. i.e., prefer replica regions first.

erin: Action items: @ajay perf run + shard sizing (due Thu), @lucy test harness + traffic profile (due Thu), @noah failure-mode runbook + fallback sequencing (due Fri), @maya draft contract fallback wording and SLA exceptions (due Fri). I'll consolidate into PRD and push for review.

deploy-bot: Document created: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/dedicated-capacity/sla-2023456789 (auto)

erin: Thanks everyone — please add small comments inline on the PRD doc. If we can't hit 99.95 without unreasonable cost, we should propose a tiered SLA (99.9 vs 99.95) and map to dedicated pool sizes. :thumbsup:
